points.description: States the property: there is a single unique path between every pair of nodes (equivalently: loop-free subnet containing all nodes).
Explains why this suits broad/multicasting: no loops, so no unnecessary duplicate packets are distributed when forwarding along the tree.

Modification: each intermediate system/node adds its multicast group membership information to its link state packet, which is distributed network-wide (because a node initially only knows its own groups).
points.partial_credit: Half if only says group information is added to LSPs but not that it is flooded/distributed to all nodes or why.

points.description: Once the full topology and group information are known locally at every node, each node computes the multicast spanning tree itself using a spanning tree algorithm such as Prim or Kruskal.
points.partial_credit: Half if says each node computes the tree locally from complete information but names no algorithm or gives a wrong one.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all four elements stated precisely: the unique-path/loop-free property, the no-duplicates reason, multicast group info added to link state packets and distributed, and local tree computation (Prim/Kruskal) from complete information. Vague statements such as "it is efficient" or "use link state routing" earn nothing for the point. A wrong statement within a point (e.g. the tree contains loops, or the tree is computed centrally) cancels that point.
